task-139 cash-item-use-pet-skill coverage sweep (IDA session e4abcb98, GMS_v95), re-deriving and confirming the final-review partial finding at the same addresses. CWvsContext::SendConsumeCashItemUseRequest @0x9eb3e0 dispatches a switch on get_consume_cash_item_type(itemId) through a byte-indirected jump table (range check @0x9eb4fd 'ja def_9EB50A'; table @0x9eb50a). Type 28 IS uniquely dispatched (label $LN2090_1 @0x9f06be), but its FULL body is: lea this,[var_208] (var_208 is typed ZArray<unsigned char> and sits immediately after the 'oPacket' stack slot — the packet's own backing byte buffer); call ZArray<unsigned char>::RemoveAll() @0x9f06c9 (discards whatever bytes were already encoded, i.e. the pre-switch common header: opcode + Encode2(nPOS) + Encode4(nItemID)); call ZXString<char>::~ZXString<char>() @0x9f06e0; jmp loc_9EB68E @0x9f06e5 — which is the function's OWN EPILOGUE (SEH restore, register pops, retn 0x10). There is no Encode2/Encode4/Encode8/EncodeBuffer/EncodeStr call anywhere in the arm and no SendPacket call is reachable from it. Net effect: selecting a type-28 cash item on gms_v95 sends NOTHING on the wire, not even the common header — behaviorally equivalent to v72/v79/v83/v84/v87's absent case-28 arm, not a partially-built codec. Recorded n-a (not left incomplete) because there is no payload — petId, locker-SN, or otherwise — that a future verify pass could ever fixture from this arm; see docs/tasks/task-139-pet-auto-pot-validation/cash-item-use-pet-skill-coverage.md for the counter-consideration (a case value IS allocated here, unlike the other GMS versions) that a future reader may weigh differently.
